title: (CS)²AI Online™ Symposium: Smart Building Cybersecurity
description:
### Panel A: When Hackers Cross into the Physical World — Ransomware and Building Systems

**Description:**
Attackers are no longer content with stealing data. In 2026 they have hacked refrigeration systems across hundreds of grocery stores, causing spoiled food and fires. They have disrupted door access and HVAC at a hospital, and they have locked staff out of their own offices to force ransom payments. Building automation systems (BAS) control HVAC, access control, lighting, elevators and fire panels. Most of them run on protocols with no authentication, and they are rarely monitored. That makes them both leverage for extortion and a hidden way into corporate IT. This panel looks at how and why attackers target buildings, what a “physical consequence” attack looks like, and what owners, operators and integrators should do now.

### Presentation: Managing Smart Building Vendors: Practical Strategies to Reduce Cybersecurity and Operational Risk

***

### Panel B: Smarter Buildings, Smarter Attackers — AI, Regulation and Accountability

**Description:**
AI is entering building operations from both directions. Operators are deploying AI agents to optimize energy, comfort and maintenance. Attackers are using AI to learn obscure embedded systems and speed up reconnaissance. At the same time, regulation is catching up: NIS2 and the EU Cyber Resilience Act are bringing BAS into compliance scope. Insurers are demanding evidence of controls, and boards are being told that cyber risk to physical operations is a governance issue. This panel examines what AI changes in building cybersecurity, how emerging rules affect owners, manufacturers and integrators, and who should be accountable when a “smart” building is compromised.

description:
Meet people and pick up your weekly groceries.

🤝 **A casual networking hangout in the grocery store cafe**
Chats, connections, & grocery carts is a relaxed, social-first networking event for curious, friendly people across Hampton Roads who enjoy good conversation and knocking out life errands at the same time.

This is not a lecture.
This is not a pitch night.
And you definitely do not need to “prepare” anything.

It is simply a low-pressure space to meet new people, have real conversations, and casually connect while wandering the aisles and picking up your weekly groceries.

Whether you are deeply into AI and automation, adjacent to tech and creativity, or just someone who enjoys thoughtful conversations with interesting humans, you belong here.

✨ **What to expect**
\- Casual\, open networking with a mix of builders\, creatives\, technologists\, founders\, students\, and professionals
\- Easy\, organic conversations while shopping at your own pace
\- Light\, optional conversation prompts to help break the ice if you want them
\- No presentations\, no panels\, no pressure to “network correctly”
\- A friendly\, welcoming environment for all backgrounds and experience levels
\- Come as you are\. Grab a cart or a basket\. Pick up dinner for the week\. \- \- Meet a few new people along the way\.

👥 **Who should attend**
Chats, Connections, & Grocery Carts is for:

People who enjoy meeting others without forced networking vibes
Builders, creatives, technologists, and curious minds
AI, automation, no-code, and tech-adjacent folks
Students and career switchers exploring what is next
Founders, consultants, operators, and professionals
Anyone who likes good conversation and low-stakes socializing

If you enjoy thoughtful chats and meeting people in unexpected places, you will fit right in.

🏪 **Why a grocery store**
You were probably going to the store anyway.

Hosting this event in a grocery store keeps things human, practical, and approachable. It removes the pressure of traditional networking and turns it into something simple, efficient, and a little fun.

Two errands. One cart.

💡 **Why this event exists**
Community grows best in relaxed, everyday spaces.

Chats, Connections, & Grocery Carts exists to create an easy, human-centered way for people to connect without titles, talks, or expectations. It is about building relationships, sharing ideas naturally, and strengthening the local community one conversation at a time.

Come say hi. Leave with groceries. Make a few new connections along the way.

# 🚀 Mission Control: Pitch, Explore & Collaborate

**Bring your curiosity. Share your ideas. Find your crew. ☄️**
Welcome to **Mission Control**, the official kickoff of **The Next Frontier 2026**, a community-driven space innovation hackathon hosted by AI Collective Hampton Roads!
This is where ideas begin to take shape.
Have an idea for an app, scientific research tool, AI project, or creative solution? Maybe you've identified a problem but aren't sure how to solve it. Or perhaps you're simply curious about science and technology and want to explore what's possible.
**You don't need a polished pitch, a finished concept, or even a team to participate!**
During this interactive kickoff, we'll:

* 🚀 **Pitch Our Rough Ideas:** Share early concepts, scientific questions, or problems you'd love to solve.
* 💡 **Brainstorm Together:** Bounce ideas off fellow innovators, exchange perspectives, and discover possibilities you might not have considered.
* 🤝 **Find Your Crew:** Meet potential collaborators with complementary skills, interests, and expertise.
* 🔭 **Explore the Challenge:** Learn about The Next Frontier's mission, project expectations, resources, and opportunities.
* 🛠️ **Prepare to Build:** Refine your concept, identify next steps, and leave with a clearer direction for your project.

Whether you're a student, scientist, developer, designer, entrepreneur, or someone who simply loves asking questions, there's a place for you at Mission Control.
**The goal isn't to arrive with the perfect idea. It's to discover what your idea could become through collaboration.**

title: WSDG November Technical Presentation
description:
Detection and Notification Case Studies
by Glover Barker

Abstract:
An overview will be provided of three different domains in which a system is monitored for problems and the user is notified, and the user must respond. Commonalities and differences will be discussed. The domains are: Network Malware Filtering and Scanning, Airport Traffic Conflict Detection, and Intravenous Infiltration Monitoring.

Bio:
Glover Barker is a retired Software Architect. His background includes software development in C++, Python, and various other languages. He has also worked in management, requirements, design, testing, quality assurance, and configuration management. Past companies include ivWatch, NASA contractors, Symantec, R. R. Donnelley, Reuters, and AT&T Bell Laboratories.

title: Cybersecurity - Chesapeake Weekend Afternoon Networking (WAN)
description:
### **Moved to Tap It Local in Chesapeake**

## **Attention Information Security and Cybersecurity Professionals!**

Are you looking to meet new people who share your interests? Whether you're considering a career in cybersecurity, just getting started, or are a seasoned professional, we welcome everyone for an evening of networking, learning, and great conversation.

### **Why Attend?**

Join us at **Tap-It Local** in Chesapeake for a relaxed evening of networking with fellow IT and cybersecurity professionals. Connect with like-minded individuals, exchange ideas, and build lasting professional relationships. Whether you enjoy a cold beer or prefer something non-alcoholic, you'll find a welcoming community eager to share experiences and knowledge.

### **About ISSA-HR**

The Information Systems Security Association of Hampton Roads (ISSA-HR) hosts networking and educational events throughout the region, bringing together cybersecurity professionals, students, and enthusiasts to share ideas, learn from one another, and grow the local cybersecurity community. Our mission is to promote the cybersecurity profession while supporting and mentoring the next generation of security professionals.

### **RSVP now and bring a friend!**

We look forward to seeing you there!
📍 **Location:** Tap-It Local
648 Grassfield Pkwy #12, Chesapeake, VA 23323
🕕 **Time:** 6:00 PM – 8:00 PM
